name: Mod Performance Monitor
summary: Shows what each mod's UI and game scripts cost, their peaks and the hitches they cause
description:
For mod makers and players who want to know which mod costs frame time. A stopwatch button at the top left, next to the data layers button, opens the Mod Performance window at the top of the screen. It times the UI scripts of every mod (and of the game itself) and credits each piece to the mod whose code it is: how long a window or HUD element takes to build, its per-frame steps, timers and event handlers, and the game's windows and functions a mod replaces or wraps.

The window shows frames per second, how much of each frame all mods take together, the game speed (how much game time passes per real second; the game lowers a chosen 2× or 4× to what its simulation can keep up with, while the speed buttons keep showing the chosen speed, so a slow "fastest" is the simulation's own cost), a line of the simulation's own timings (its update time per step, the share of real time it spends in its steps, so you can see whether the simulation itself is the limit, and the sync time between the interface and the simulation), and a row per mod, heaviest first: time per frame with a bar, its worst frame in the last 2 seconds and calls per frame. Green, yellow and red mark what is fine, worth a look and costly; mods that ran nothing are greyed out. Click a mod to see its heaviest pieces by name. Badges show a mod's game scripts and the game functions it wraps. Work done straight from a click, a table sort or a filter isn't timed. Below, the last hitches (frames of 50 ms or more that stand out from the usual frame, or where UI scripts took 20 ms) name the mods that took the most of them and the longest single call. Measuring can be stopped, and peaks and hitches reset.

Game Script Timing also times every mod's game scripts, the part of a mod that runs in the simulation. The Sim column shows each mod's time in ms per real second over the last 30 seconds, a click on the mod its heaviest functions with their longest recent call, and the simulation line how much of the simulation's time all mods' game scripts take. Game script code that runs in the interface isn't timed. Its totals are kept in your save (a few KB) and dropped by the game once the mod is removed.

The monitor adds a small cost of its own, shown in the window. Leave it off when you aren't looking for something: switch it off in the mod's Settings (the gear next to the mod when choosing a game's mods), where Hitch Log also writes the hitches to the game log (stdout.txt, at most one line a second) and once a minute the game speed and the game scripts' time, to send to a mod's author, and Logging writes the mod's own messages there for bug reports.

params.name: Monitor
params.tooltip: Times every mod's UI scripts and shows them in the Mod Performance window (stopwatch button at the top left). Off: nothing is timed.

params.name: Game Script Timing
params.tooltip: With Monitor On: also times every mod's game scripts, the part of a mod that runs in the simulation, and shows them in the window's Sim column, in ms per real second. Their totals are kept in the save (a few KB). Off: game scripts aren't timed.

params.name: Hitch Log
params.tooltip: Writes each hitch (a frame of 50 ms or more that stands out) to the game log (stdout.txt) with the mods that took the most of it, at most one line a second, and once a minute a count of the slow frames, the game speed (game time per real second, the engine's speed and its estimated maximum) and the simulation's timings.

params.name: Logging
params.tooltip: Writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt), for bug reports.
